decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the sole crash to plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call in SessionProgressBar, grounded in the console excerpt line (client.js:219:41) and both contract excerpts showing the alpha.2 kit drops that hook while useSessions and useSessionStatus persist; explicitly clears plugin B.

Explains the shared DrawerErrorBoundary over all input.dock DockEntry children, null fallback unmounting the whole subtree, cites both the render-tree note and the console 'unmounted entries' log line, and attributes the surviving attach button to the separate input.left slot with its own boundary.

Correctly bounds what the disable-experiment proves (A caused the unmount; B renders once freed) and what it does not (B's full alpha.2 compatibility; that the strip crash is the only dock defect); explains reinstalling B was pointless because B was never broken, and refutes the colleague theory since B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Provides corrected fenced code reading pending state via useSessionStatus(...)?.pendingInteraction-derived map with optional chaining and an empty-map fallback, states which features degrade (pending indicators only) and which keep working (running, todos, tokens, ETA via unchanged useSessions/useConversation/useProjection), and justifies silent degradation because a throw unmounts co-tenants under the shared boundary.

Verification is refresh-based without host restart, requires both entries rendered together with zero errors, and covers B's paste/remove/re-paste regression with A enabled; hygiene covers defensive destructuring, a local per-entry boundary, and the host per-entry-boundary trade-off of blast-radius isolation versus a loud single signal.

caps.reason: The final remedy rewrites plugin A's SessionProgressBar to use useSessionStatus; plugin B needs no fix and the report explicitly rejects reinstalling B and the two-independent-bugs theory.
